units.text: EXT. PUBLIC BOCCE COURT - TWILIGHT
A crushed-oyster-shell lane between two wooden rails.
String lights droop from a mulberry tree.
A cooler of beer rests on a bench.
The last frame of a long match.
Four players stand at the near end.
NONNA ALBERTINA FERRANTE-OKOYE (70s, apron over Sunday dress) holds a red ball, rolling it in her palm.
Her partner, SALVATORE "SAL THE HAND" DRUMMOND (60s, straw hat, cigar unlit) leans on his cane.

Their rivals: WALTER BRENNAN-ISHIDA (60s, golf visor) stands rigid with a green ball, and his daughter CLEMENTINE (30s, headphones around her neck) chews a toothpick and watches the pallino sitting at the far end.
Everybody quiet.
units.name: ALBERTINA

units.text: We're quiet.
units.name: SAL

units.text: I'm not breathing.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Dad, you're breathing.
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: Albertina steps to the line.
Bends her knees.
Swings.
The red ball rolls, wobbles, bumps a rail, slows, and kisses the pallino.
A hush.
Then it rolls on, a quarter inch, and drifts to a stop precisely against it.
Did you see that? Did you all see that?
units.name: SAL

units.text: I saw it.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: We all saw it.
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: Walter lays his green ball gently on the bench.
He pulls off his visor, wipes his forehead with the back of his wrist, and puts it on again, backward.
Walter. Fine game.
units.name: ALBERTINA

units.text: Albertina. Fifty years I've wanted to say that to you.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Say what?
units.name: ALBERTINA

units.text: Fine game.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: They shake hands.
Sal lights the cigar at last.
Clementine looks at the pallino, at the red ball against it, at her father's backward visor, and begins, helplessly, to laugh.
